name: Degradation-evidence codebook of the wheeled-robot autonomy survey

versions.note: First version, fixed before any work was coded. Both coding passes used it.

Written after the agreement step. response_family holds the primary family only (CR20). drivetrain_effect excludes differences between wheeled and other locomotion, actuator or speed limits that apply to any wheel arrangement, and kinematic models without a reported geometry-dependent result. The adjudication log adds recheck-revised and multi-part deciding locators. No allowed value, sampling rule, agreement unit or derived measure changed.

coding_unit.rule: Each work in the survey selection is coded once. Every attribute summarizes all experiments that the publication reports. The strongest value across experiments is coded where an attribute has an order.
coding_unit.same_experiment_rule: A conjunction attribute (deg_task_class, deg_task_setting) counts only when its two parts occur in the same experiment: the same trial set, results table or results figure. Its locator names that table, figure or trial set.
coding_unit.experiment: A set of runs or evaluations of one system configuration family under one protocol whose results are reported together in a table, a figure or a numbered result paragraph.
coding_unit.any_experiment_variant: The sensitivity analysis S-unit-any relaxes the same-experiment rule and lets the two parts come from different experiments of the publication.

inputs: transcription of the publication (02-fulltext/<theme>/<folder>/paper.md, local only)
batch reading records (06-data/<batch>/source-reading.json), primary coder only

verification_levels.full: The whole paper was read and every number of the card was checked against the paper.
verification_levels.light: A targeted reading or a converted legacy extraction. Its statements need a page-located check before a number from it is cited.

evidence_base.numbers_rule: Codes are categorical. A number taken from a light card is cited in the survey only after a page-located check against the PDF.
evidence_base.card_fields_rule: Card fields degradation, degradation_observed, evaluation_all and secondary_modules are candidate values. They do not separate the three evidence classes or test the same-experiment rule, so the coder decides each value from the card text, the transcription or the PDF.

file_format.csv: UTF-8 without BOM, LF line endings, header row equal to columns; multi-valued fields joined with '|' in canonical order; an empty set is written 'none'.

functions.name: Localization and mapping
functions.scope: State estimation, odometry, SLAM, relocalization, map building and map maintenance, and datasets for these tasks.

functions.name: Traversability, planning and control
functions.scope: Traversability assessment, exploration planning, global and local motion planning, tracking control, learned local motion and crowd navigation.

functions.name: Semantic and language-guided navigation
functions.scope: Semantic maps and memory, open-vocabulary and language-conditioned navigation, vision-language models in the motion loop, and semantically driven social navigation.

functions.name: Multi-robot coordination
functions.scope: Two or more robots that exchange information or coordinate: exploration, collaborative SLAM, map merging, cooperative localization, task allocation and formation control.

functions.name: Fault tolerance, recovery and long-term deployment
functions.scope: Localization integrity, fault detection and isolation, fault-tolerant control, recovery behaviors, runtime monitoring, energy and long-term deployment.

principal_section_rule: The principal section is the card field survey_module mapped to its section (IV-VIII). The context review takes 'context'. A work keeps exactly one principal section, which decides where the survey discusses it and which column of the source-by-function matrix it occupies.
multi_cell_rule: A work occupies one matrix cell for every source in src_addressed, all in the column of its principal section. In the function-pair co-occurrence matrix it counts once in every unordered pair of distinct functions in its functions list. Cell totals therefore exceed the number of works.

sources.name: Perceptual degradation
sources.rule: The environment makes measurements uninformative: illumination change, darkness, low texture, motion blur, glare, smoke, dust, fog, rain or snow that degrade sensing, geometric degeneracy, sparse or missing returns, GNSS outage or multipath, and a sensor dropout whose cause the paper does not state.

sources.name: Sensor fault and false association
sources.rule: A sensor or an association step produces wrong data: sensor failure, bias, drift beyond specification, frozen or corrupted output, spoofing or other attack, and wrong or missing feature, landmark or place association.

sources.name: Terrain and wheel-ground contact
sources.rule: The ground departs from flat, rigid support with known contact: uneven, rough, sloped, vegetated or deformable ground, negative obstacles, wheel slip, skidding and wheel-ground model mismatch.

sources.name: Actuator fault and saturation
sources.rule: Commanded motion is not delivered: loss of actuator effectiveness, actuator bias, saturation, a stuck or failed wheel, motor or steering unit.

sources.name: Moving agents
sources.rule: Pedestrians, vehicles, animals or uncoordinated robots move in the scene and the study treats them as a disturbance, predicts or avoids them, or varies them. Robots coordinated by the evaluated method are not moving agents of this source.

sources.name: Map and scene change
sources.rule: A map or prior no longer matches the scene: map aging, layout change, relocated semi-static objects, seasonal or long-term change and a deliberately altered prior map. Exploring an unknown but static scene is not map change.

sources.name: Learned and semantic inference error
sources.rule: A learned or foundation model gives wrong output: misclassification, misgrounding, a wrong or invented language-model response, unreliable learned predictions and out-of-distribution inputs. Using a learned model does not by itself code this source.

sources.name: Communication loss, delay and bandwidth
sources.rule: Information between robots, or between a robot and a server or cloud service, arrives late, out of order, incompletely or not at all: delay, jitter, packet loss, partition or disconnection and limited data rate.

sources.name: Computation and energy limits
sources.rule: Limited onboard processing, memory or inference time, including the time a remote model takes to answer once a request has arrived, and battery or charging constraints. Network transfer time belongs to COM.

assumptions.statement: Measurements are informative and correctly associated.
Wheels roll on supporting ground with known contact.
The mapped scene is static or persistent.
Learned and semantic inference is valid.
Shared information is timely and consistent.
Actuation, computation and energy remain available.

assumption_link_rule: The response families listed per assumption are the links stated before coding. The links drawn in the survey figure are recounted from coded works as pairs of an addressed source and the work's primary response family, and a link is drawn only when at least one coded work supports it.

response_families.name: Localizability and selective measurement updates
response_families.scope: Detect uninformative or degenerate measurements and condition, weight, select or skip the update.

response_families.name: Complementary sensing
response_families.scope: Add, switch or reweight sensing modalities so that another modality covers a degraded one.

response_families.name: Motion priors, contact and adaptation
response_families.scope: Kinematic, contact or slip models and their online adaptation inside estimation.

response_families.name: Dynamic geometry and persistent maps
response_families.scope: Remove or track moving geometry, estimate persistence and maintain maps over time.

response_families.name: Prior-map and cross-modal localization
response_families.scope: Localize or relocalize against a prior, cross-modal or global map.

response_families.name: Cooperative estimates and uncertain maps
response_families.scope: Estimation that uses other agents' estimates, external infrastructure or map priors with explicit uncertainty.

response_families.name: Terrain support and traversability costs
response_families.scope: Estimate support, traversability, terrain cost or terrain risk for planning.

response_families.name: Exploration with information and geometry
response_families.scope: Exploration planners driven by information gain, frontier structure or geometry.

response_families.name: Learning, prediction and interaction
response_families.scope: Learned planners or policies, prediction of other agents and interaction-aware planning.

response_families.name: Safety filters and explicit risk conditions
response_families.scope: Barrier functions, chance or risk constraints and other explicit safety conditions on motion.

response_families.name: Tracking, mission costs and network support
response_families.scope: Tracking control with learned or adapted dynamics, delay-aware or networked control and mission-level costs.

response_families.name: Semantic memory and scene structure
response_families.scope: Build, update and query semantic maps, scene graphs or object memory.

response_families.name: Geographic grounding, priors and learned actions
response_families.scope: Ground instructions in maps or geography, use semantic priors, or let a learned model output actions.

response_families.name: Candidate selection and behavioral constraints
response_families.scope: A model selects among candidates that geometric modules generate or check, or social and behavioral constraints shape motion.

response_families.name: Memory, timing and embodied execution
response_families.scope: Query timing, latency handling, memory horizons and execution of model decisions on a robot.

response_families.name: Task allocation and spatial responsibility
response_families.scope: Assign tasks, regions or goals among robots.

response_families.name: Compact sharing and distributed estimation
response_families.scope: Select, compress or schedule shared data and estimate jointly with distributed inference.

response_families.name: Rendezvous, disconnection and conditional repair
response_families.scope: Plan reconnection, operate through partitions and repair shared estimates after faults or reconnection.

response_families.name: Motion interaction and persistent service
response_families.scope: Formation, inter-robot motion coordination and persistent multi-robot service.

response_families.name: Fault estimation and tolerant control
response_families.scope: Estimate faults and keep control performance under them.

response_families.name: Integrity and failure monitoring
response_families.scope: Bound hazardous error, predict or detect failure and monitor runtime validity.

response_families.name: From diagnosis to an executed response
response_families.scope: Select and execute a recovery or fallback action after a detected failure.

response_families.name: Resources and sustained operation
response_families.scope: Energy, charging, service scheduling and long-duration deployment.

response_families.name: Dataset or benchmark resource
response_families.scope: The main contribution is a dataset or benchmark (card evidence_type dataset-resource).

response_families.name: Context review
response_families.scope: The single literature review kept for context.

evidence_classes.name: Injected or varied degradation with a comparator
evidence_classes.rule: The authors inject, impose, remove or vary the condition while the task setup stays otherwise the same (same course, scene, sequence or simulated world), and report the same system at a second level of the condition (nominal or another severity), or report the same system with and without the evaluated response under the same injected condition.

evidence_classes.name: Deliberately selected difficult condition without manipulation
evidence_classes.rule: The authors include the condition on purpose for its difficulty without controlling its level (chosen sequences, sites, routes, crowds, or a dataset built to contain it), or they inject or impose it but report the same system at one level only with no with-and-without comparison (single_level_injection = yes).

evidence_classes.name: Incidental degradation
evidence_classes.rule: The condition occurred during an experiment and the paper reports it (failure analysis, field notes, limitations that refer to observed runs), but the evaluation did not include it on purpose.

class_rules.per_source: Each source enters at most one of src_manipulated, src_selected and src_incidental, namely the strongest class it reaches in any experiment (D1 > D2 > D3).
class_rules.publication_class: The strongest class over all sources (D1 > D2 > D3 > none).
class_rules.named_condition: A named degradation condition is a source coded D1 or D2.
class_rules.motivation_only: A condition that appears only as motivation, related work or future work is not coded in any class column.
class_rules.comparator: A comparison against other methods at one level of an injected condition is not a comparator. A baseline counts as the same system without the response when the paper states that the proposed system is that baseline plus the response (an ablation or the base pipeline it extends).
class_rules.simulation: Injection or variation in simulation is D1 when the comparator rule holds. The setting is recorded in level_degradation and deg_task_setting, not in the class.
class_rules.different_sites: Results on different sites, routes or sequences chosen for different conditions are D2, also when a nominal sequence is reported beside them, since other factors change with the condition. A recording counts as controlled only when the authors, or the documented design of the dataset, changed the condition alone between the compared recordings (same route, rig and scene).
class_rules.domain_shift: A sim-to-real or cross-domain test of a learned model is D2 for MOD when its results are reported separately. A standard held-out test split is not a named condition.
class_rules.dataset_resource: A dataset or benchmark built to contain a condition codes that condition D2, also without an evaluated method.
class_rules.moving_agents: Moving agents are D1 when their number, density, speed or behavior is varied with a comparator, D2 when a crowded site or scripted crossing is chosen without a comparator, and D3 when passers-by occur in a run and the paper reports their effect.

evidence_levels.name: Resource or review without a ranked setting

shade_steps: replay, simulation, numerical model or resource

platform_groups.name: Non-ground, handheld, mixed-carrier or no platform

transfer_criteria: The inputs of the mechanism exist on a wheeled ground robot.
The assumptions of the mechanism do not rest on the other embodiment (legs, flight, water, a handheld carrier or road-vehicle infrastructure).
The evaluation isolates the mechanism from the platform-specific parts of the system.

depth_rule.light-legacy: verification_level = light and source_batch in legacy_batches
depth_rule.light-targeted: verification_level = light and source_batch not in legacy_batches
depth_rule.locator_consequence: A light-legacy card carries few page citations, so every value that needs a locator also needs a transcription or PDF locator.

stage_groups.quota_rule: Stages whose selection basis fixed an equal number of works per theme (ten and six per theme).

attributes.name: code
attributes.derivation: Library code of the work (06-data/survey-inclusion.json selected_ids).
attributes.rule: Copied, never coded.

attributes.name: principal_section
attributes.derivation: Card survey_module mapped through functions[].module; 'context' when survey_included = context.
attributes.rule: Copied, never coded.

attributes.name: stage
attributes.derivation: source_batch of 06-data/paper-index.csv.
attributes.rule: Copied, never coded.

attributes.name: depth
attributes.derivation: depth_rule applied to verification_level and source_batch.
attributes.rule: Copied, never coded.

attributes.name: functions
attributes.derivation: Candidates: survey_module plus secondary_modules of the card.
attributes.rule: Always include the principal function. Add another function when the work contributes or modifies a component that performs it, when its mechanism takes that function's output quality, uncertainty or failure state as an explicit input and changes behavior accordingly, or when its evaluation reports a measure of that function as an outcome of the mechanism. An unmodified off-the-shelf module needed only to run the experiment does not count, nor does a function named only as motivation or future work. MRC requires two or more robots that exchange information or coordinate inside the mechanism. 'none' only for the context review.
attributes.locator: One locator for every function other than the principal one.

attributes.name: src_addressed
attributes.derivation: Candidates: degradation and degradation_observed of the card, mapped through sources[].vocabulary, and the card Problem block.
attributes.rule: Every source whose degradation the mechanism, or the resource, is designed to tolerate, detect, bound or recover from, as stated in the problem statement, the mechanism or the contribution list, plus every source in src_manipulated and src_selected. 'none' is expected only for the context review and for a resource that targets no source; any other 'none' needs a note that names the stated problem and why no source applies.
attributes.locator: One locator for every listed source.

attributes.name: response_family
attributes.derivation: No card field. The primary coder may start from the survey subsection that first cites the work.
attributes.rule: A primary family from the principal section that matches the response the work contributes, chosen by the main claim of the abstract or contribution list. 'resource' is the primary family of a dataset or benchmark resource and 'context' that of the context review. Version 1.0 allowed an optional secondary family after '|'. From version 1.1 the final codes hold the primary family only (CR20); the form stays one-or-two so that the version 1.0 records validate.
attributes.locator: One locator for every listed family.

attributes.name: src_manipulated
attributes.derivation: Candidates: card degradation (does not separate D1 from D2).
attributes.rule: Sources whose strongest class is D1.
attributes.locator: One locator per source naming the comparison (table, figure or trial set).

attributes.name: src_selected
attributes.derivation: Candidates: card degradation.
attributes.rule: Sources whose strongest class is D2.
attributes.locator: One locator per source naming the selected sequence, site or condition.

attributes.name: src_incidental
attributes.derivation: Candidates: card degradation_observed.
attributes.rule: Sources whose strongest class is D3.
attributes.locator: One locator per source naming the report of the occurrence.

attributes.name: nominal_control
attributes.derivation: No card field.
attributes.rule: 'yes' when at least one D1 comparison includes a level at which the condition is absent. 'no' when every D1 comparison is between non-nominal levels or is a with-and-without-response comparison under the injected condition. 'na' when src_manipulated is none.

attributes.name: single_level_injection
attributes.derivation: No card field.
attributes.rule: 'yes' when the authors inject or impose a condition but report the same system at that one level only, with no with-and-without-response comparison, so that the source is coded D2.

attributes.name: task_setting
attributes.derivation: Candidates: closed-loop-task in the card evaluation_all, evidence_all and protocol_caveats.
attributes.rule: Settings in which the work reports a task outcome. A task outcome is a mission-level result of closed-loop execution: success or failure, goal arrival, collisions or safety-constraint violations, coverage or explored area, completion or traversal time, distance travelled, interventions or service availability. Estimation, tracking and prediction errors are component measures, also when measured in closed loop. 'physical' needs a numeric outcome from physical runs in text or a table; a video or a plot without stated numbers does not count. Physics simulation and closed-loop numerical models are 'simulation'.
attributes.locator: One locator for any value other than 'none'.

attributes.name: deg_task_class
attributes.derivation: No card field. The card combination of a degradation condition and closed-loop-task does not test the same experiment.
attributes.rule: The strongest class of a named condition that occurs in the same experiment as a task outcome. 'D1' when the task outcome itself is reported for the same system at two levels of a manipulated condition, or with and without the response under it. 'D2' when the task outcome is reported under a selected condition, or under a manipulated condition without a task-level comparator.
attributes.locator: One locator naming the table, figure or trial set that holds both parts.

attributes.name: deg_task_setting
attributes.derivation: No card field.
attributes.rule: 'physical' when at least one same-experiment conjunction of deg_task_class ran on a physical robot, otherwise 'simulation'. 'none' exactly when deg_task_class is none.
attributes.locator: One locator for any value other than 'none'.

attributes.name: level_strongest
attributes.derivation: Card evidence_type mapped through evidence_levels.
attributes.rule: Copied from the card. A coder who finds the card value contradicted by the paper keeps the derived value and writes the discrepancy in notes.

attributes.name: level_degradation
attributes.derivation: Candidate when evidence_all of the card has one setting.
attributes.rule: Evidence level of the strongest experiment that reports a result under a named condition (D1 or D2). 'X' for a resource that contains the condition without an evaluated method; a resource that evaluates baseline methods on its own recordings takes 'R'. A physical run without a stated result (video only) does not raise the level. 'none' when no source is coded D1 or D2.
attributes.locator: One locator for any value other than 'none'.

attributes.name: integrity
attributes.derivation: 'yes' when the card evaluation_all contains integrity-reliability.
attributes.rule: Copied from the card; discrepancies go to notes.

attributes.name: placement_reported
attributes.derivation: 'yes' when the card compute_location is neither not-reported nor not-applicable.
attributes.rule: Copied from the card; discrepancies go to notes.

attributes.name: platform_group
attributes.derivation: Card platform_class mapped through platform_groups.
attributes.rule: Copied from the card; discrepancies go to notes.

attributes.name: mixed_wheeled
attributes.derivation: Card platform free text when platform_class is mixed.
attributes.rule: 'yes' when a mixed-carrier dataset or study includes a wheeled ground robot among its carriers, 'no' when it does not or the carriers are unidentified, 'na' when platform_class is not mixed.

attributes.name: drivetrain
attributes.derivation: Card platform_class mapped through drivetrain_map; 'na' outside the target wheeled group.
attributes.rule: Copied from the card; discrepancies go to notes.

attributes.name: drivetrain_effect
attributes.derivation: No card field. Read Problem, Mechanism, Stated limitations and Transfer conditions, then the paper.
attributes.rule: 'yes' when the paper states or shows, in the design rationale, the results or the limitations, that a degradation effect or the feasibility of a response depends on the wheel arrangement or steering geometry of a wheeled platform: skid-steer slip in turns, minimum turning radius or non-holonomic limits of car-like steering, lateral motion of omnidirectional bases, reversing limits, rotation in place or footprint. Naming the drivetrain or using a generic kinematic model without a reported effect is 'no'. Coded for every work, including works outside the target wheeled group that report such an effect for a wheeled carrier. Version 1.1: the attribute compares wheel arrangements and steering geometries among wheeled carriers. A difference between wheeled and legged or other locomotion, an actuator or speed limit that applies to any wheel arrangement, and a controller built on a drivetrain-specific kinematic model without a reported geometry-dependent result or design choice are 'no'. Wheels repositioned to reshape the support footprint, a differential base that cannot strafe and a design built around the minimum turning radius remain 'yes'.

attributes.name: transfer_basis
attributes.derivation: Card Transfer conditions block; inclusion rule of 06-data/vocabulary.md.
attributes.rule: For works outside the target wheeled group: 'mechanism' when all three transfer_criteria hold, 'counterexample' when the work shows where wheeled transfer would break, with a note naming the failed criterion. 'na' for target wheeled works and the context review.
attributes.locator: One locator for any value other than 'na'.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.derivation: Free text.
attributes.rule: Short English text without quotations of publisher text. The tag 'human-assistance' marks a work whose response or evaluation relies on human intervention, takeover or remote supervision.

consistency_rules.rule: functions contains the principal function; it is 'none' only for the context review.
src_addressed contains every source of src_manipulated and src_selected.
src_manipulated, src_selected and src_incidental share no source.
nominal_control is 'na' exactly when src_manipulated is none.
single_level_injection 'yes' requires a source in src_selected.
deg_task_class 'D1' requires a source in src_manipulated; 'D2' requires a source in src_manipulated or src_selected.
deg_task_setting is 'none' exactly when deg_task_class is 'none'.
deg_task_setting 'physical' requires task_setting 'physical' or 'both'; 'simulation' requires task_setting 'simulation' or 'both'.
level_degradation is 'none' exactly when src_manipulated and src_selected are both none.
deg_task_setting 'physical' requires level_degradation 'P'.
level_degradation does not outrank level_strongest unless level_strongest is 'X'.
The primary response family belongs to the principal section, or is 'resource' for a resource (level_strongest 'X') or 'context' for the context review; a secondary family differs from the primary.
src_addressed 'none' for a technical work that is not a resource needs a note.
mixed_wheeled is 'na' exactly when the card platform_class is not mixed.
transfer_basis is 'na' exactly when platform_group is 'WHL' or the work is the context review.
Given and derived attributes equal their derivation.
Every value that the locator rules require has a locator row; for a light-legacy work at least one of them has source 'pdf' or 'transcription'.
Multi-valued fields list each id once, in canonical order.
The context review codes none or na in every coded attribute except response_family 'context' and drivetrain_effect 'no'.
From version 1.1, response_family in the final codes holds one family. The check applies to the final codes, not to the frozen version 1.0 records.

formats.pdf: PDF p. N, the physical page of the PDF file counted from 1, optionally followed by a table, figure or section label (PDF p. 7, Table II)
formats.card: card: <block name>, optionally with the page that the card cites (card: Baselines and controls, p. 6)
formats.transcription: transcription: <section heading, table or figure label>
formats.source-reading: source-reading: <page scope or excerpt label of the batch reading record>

locator_rules.light_cards: For a light card, a card locator suffices only when the cited card passage names a page. A light-legacy card always needs a pdf or transcription locator in addition.
locator_rules.no_quotation: Locators and notes paraphrase. They never copy publisher text.
locator_rules.value_field: For a multi-valued attribute the locator row names one id; for a single-valued attribute it names the coded value.

derived_measures.publication_class: Strongest of D1 (src_manipulated not none), D2 (src_selected not none), D3 (src_incidental not none), otherwise none.
derived_measures.headline: deg_task_class is D1 or D2: a named degradation condition and a task outcome in the same experiment.
derived_measures.direct_wheeled_joint: deg_task_class is D1 or D2, deg_task_setting is physical and platform_group is WHL.
derived_measures.shares: Shares are reported per principal section (function) over the technical works of that section and pooled over all technical works. Every share is a statistic of the purposively selected sample, not an estimate of prevalence in the literature.

matrix.rows: The nine sources in source_order, grouped by assumption A1-A6.
matrix.cell: a = works in the column with the source in src_addressed; n = works with the source in named_sources; m = works with the source in src_manipulated; k = target wheeled works among the a works; counts of the a works in ROAD, GND and OTH shown by their marks.
matrix.shade: Shade step of the strongest level_degradation among the n works (shade_steps).

cooccurrence.pairs: Unordered pairs {a, b} of distinct functions.
cooccurrence.works: Works whose functions contain both a and b.
cooccurrence.joint_named_same: Of these, works with deg_task_class D1 or D2.
cooccurrence.joint_manipulated_same: Of these, works with deg_task_class D1.
cooccurrence.joint_physical_named: Of these, works with deg_task_class D1 or D2 and deg_task_setting physical.
cooccurrence.direct_wheeled_joint: Of these, joint_physical_named works in platform_group WHL.
cooccurrence.wheeled_works: Works of the pair in platform_group WHL.
cooccurrence.strongest_level: Strongest level_degradation among the works of the pair.

interface_ranking.candidate: An unordered pair of distinct functions {f, g} with one coupling source s. Its works W are the works whose functions contain f and g and whose src_addressed or named_sources or src_incidental contain s.
interface_ranking.candidate_id: <f>-<g>:<s> with f before g in function order (LOC, PLN, SEM, MRC, REL).

metrics.j: Works of W with deg_task_class D1 or D2, deg_task_setting physical and platform_group WHL (direct joint wheeled evidence).
metrics.w: Works of W in platform_group WHL.
metrics.safety_relevant: PLN or REL is one of f and g.

interfaces.name: Pose uncertainty in wheeled terrain decisions
Disconnection, reconnection and corrupted shared information

interface_ranking.interface_rank: The best rank among the eligible admissible cells of the interface.

named_alternatives.name: Energy or computation limits on planning
Human assistance
named_alternatives.count_rule: Outside the function-pair scheme; reported as the number of works whose notes carry the tag human-assistance.

sensitivity_rankings.rule: Recompute W, the metrics and the ranks without the works of the integration-questions stage, which was acquired for the four interfaces.
Sort by gap_share descending, then by the same tie-breaks.

interface_ranking.reporting_rule: Every candidate that ranks above the lowest-ranked developed interface is listed with a reason for not developing it. If the four interfaces are not the four highest-ranked candidates, the survey states this and keeps the four as an agenda proposed by this survey.

sensitivity.rule: deg_task_class D1 and nominal_control yes (publication-level control, so the nominal level may belong to another experiment).
deg_task_class D1 or D2 and deg_task_setting physical.
Headline, or src_incidental not none in a work that reports a task outcome.
named_sources not none and task_setting not none, without the same-experiment rule.
Card coding of the previous revision: evaluation_all contains both designed-degradation and closed-loop-task.

sensitivity.subset: All technical works except those of one stage; one row per stage in stage_order.
bibliographic_year in one year band; one row per year_bands entry.
Quota stages and theme folder T1-T6; one row per theme.
stage is not the coverage-additions stage

sensitivity_reporting: Each row reports numerator, denominator and pooled share, and the share per function (LOC, PLN, SEM, MRC, REL). Definition and coding-unit rows use all technical works; subset rows use the headline definition.

findings.statement: LOC has the lowest headline share among the five functions.
findings.test: share(LOC) <= share(f) for every other function f; ties are reported.

findings.statement: REL has the highest headline share among the five functions.
findings.test: share(REL) >= share(f) for every other function f; ties are reported.

findings.statement: Task outcomes appear in at least 90% of PLN works and of SEM works.
findings.test: task_outcome share >= 0.90 in PLN and in SEM.

findings.statement: Task outcomes appear in at most 5% of LOC works.

findings_rule: A robustness row states for each subset and definition whether each finding holds. A finding is 'n/a' in a subset where a function it compares has fewer than 3 works. Definition rows change RF1 and RF2 only.

double_coding.coder: An independent language-model session on a different model from the primary coder, with no access to the primary codes.
double_coding.not_double_coded_reason: Given and derived attributes copy or map card fields that both coders read, so their agreement would be trivial. mixed_wheeled and transfer_basis are single-coded descriptors of the platform.

statistics.measure: Cohen's kappa per function over the sampled works whose principal function differs from it, and exact-set agreement over all sampled works.
Cohen's kappa per source flag and exact-set agreement.
Cohen's kappa of the primary family.
Cohen's kappa per source flag (D1 or D2) and exact-set agreement.
Pooled Cohen's kappa over the nine source flags of every sampled work, and exact-set agreement.
Cohen's kappa over D1, D2, D3 and none.

double_coding.kappa: Unweighted Cohen's kappa (po - pe) / (1 - pe). It is undefined when pe = 1 (both coders use one category); the report then gives 'n/a' with percent agreement and prevalence.
double_coding.percent_agreement: Share of units on which both coders give the same value.
double_coding.interpretation: Both coders are language-model sessions that read the same review cards, which were themselves prepared with language-model tools. The statistic measures agreement in applying this codebook to shared evidence. It is not human inter-rater reliability.
double_coding.adjudication: Every disagreement is resolved by re-reading the source at both coders' locators and logged with the resolved value, the resolution (primary-kept, second-adopted or both-revised), a short reason and the deciding locator. A rule that causes disagreement in three or more sampled works is clarified in a new codebook version, and the pattern is rechecked across all works with every change logged. A change from that recheck has the scope corpus-recheck and the resolution recheck-revised. A deciding locator may list several locators separated by '; ', and it serves as the locator of every value that the resolution introduces.
double_coding.frozen_primary: The primary codes are frozen with a SHA-256 record before agreement is computed. Later corrections go through the adjudication log.

sampling.population: Technical works of the selection (survey_included = yes). The context review is excluded.
sampling.strata: Principal section (IV-VIII) by assessment depth (full, light-legacy, light-targeted), with selection stage as a coverage constraint.
sampling.full_rule: min(2, full works of the section).
sampling.light_rule: The remaining seats of the section are split between light-legacy and light-targeted by the largest-remainder method over their counts in the section; a tie in remainders goes to light-legacy; no stratum receives more seats than it has works.
sampling.generator: Python random.Random(seed + k) for attempt k = 0, 1, 2, ...; one generator per attempt, used for the strata in section order and, within a section, in depth order.
sampling.stratum_draw: random.Random.sample over the stratum's codes sorted in ascending order.
sampling.stage_coverage: Every selection stage with at least min_stage_size technical works appears at least once. An attempt that misses one is rejected and k increases by 1.
sampling.record: The attempt index k, every rejected attempt with its missing stages, the allocation, and per work its stratum and draw order are published after the second coding is complete. The sample list is not part of this codebook.

locators.note: planner consumes the odometry health flag
three dust densities on one course

example_cases.Z98: Fictional: a dust-tolerant LiDAR-inertial odometry method on a skid-steer robot feeds its own local planner. In a dust chamber the authors drive one course with no dust, light dust and dense dust and report trajectory error and course completion per level.
example_cases.Z99: Fictional: a localization method matches magnetometer readings against a prior magnetic-field map of an office floor and is designed to tolerate changes made after the map survey. It is evaluated only on public recordings chosen because desks and metal cabinets were moved after the survey, against other map-matching methods, with position error as the only measure.

second_coder_output.example_note: Z98 and Z99 are fictional codes. They describe no corpus work.
second_coder_output.notes_md: Session statement (host, model as the session configuration states it, date), start and end time, the SHA-256 of codebook.md as received, every file opened, every rule found ambiguous and how it was applied, and no quotation of publisher text.
